summary: The San Francisco Fed separates a broad financial-conditions index from the high-frequency policy and inflation surprises that move it. The page supports an event-study transmission node in which tightly timed rate or CPI news is linked to same-day and subsequent financial-condition changes, while the index level remains a historical standardization rather than a declaration that conditions are neutral.
question: How do monetary-policy and inflation surprises transmit into broad U.S. financial conditions over event and short post-event horizons?
horizon: announcement window through registered post-event trading days

evidence.paraphrase: The article asks how monetary-policy actions affect a weighted summary of asset prices and other financial variables that influence economic activity.
Policy surprises are measured from interest-rate changes in a narrow thirty-minute announcement window, reducing contamination by unrelated same-day news.
The empirical exercise relates identified policy and CPI surprises to changes in the financial-conditions index on the event day and subsequent days.
An index value of zero denotes its historical average, not a structural estimate of neutral financial conditions, and longer windows admit more confounding information.

variables.name: change in broad financial conditions
variables.definition: Event-to-event change in a weighted financial-conditions index summarizing rates, credit, equities, and related market prices.
variables.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco

variables.name: monetary-policy surprise
variables.definition: Unexpected policy news proxied by the change in market interest rates within a narrow FOMC announcement window.

variables.name: CPI news surprise
variables.definition: Released CPI inflation minus the pre-release survey consensus available to market participants.
variables.provider: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and survey consensus

variables.name: financial-condition components
variables.definition: Component-level rate, spread, equity, exchange-rate, and other market responses underlying the composite index.

routes.method: high-frequency event study with local post-event projections
routes.estimand: change in broad financial conditions at event horizon k per unit of identified monetary-policy or inflation surprise
routes.identification: narrow-window market surprises isolate the unexpected component of scheduled announcements under a no-concurrent-news assumption
assumptions: market prices incorporate the scheduled announcement inside the registered window
no other material news systematically coincides with the narrow window
event dates and horizons are fixed before estimation
routes.sample: registered FOMC and CPI announcement events with synchronized high-frequency market data
diagnostics: heteroskedasticity-robust or HAC covariance by horizon
joint horizon test and multiple-testing control
routes.aggregation: identified monetary-transmission evidence node feeding the financial-conditions lane

summary: The New York Fed Trend Wage Inflation framework decomposes worker-level wage growth into persistent and transitory movements and into economy-wide versus industry-specific components. For MacroTrace it is a latent-state labor-cost node with explicit uncertainty and sector heterogeneity, not a single observed wage-growth series or an unconditional claim about future price inflation.
question: What portion of current U.S. wage inflation is persistent and common across industries, and what portion is transitory or industry specific?
horizon: current latent wage trend and near-term persistence

evidence.paraphrase: The article motivates a measure that distinguishes the persistent state of wage growth from volatile worker-level observations and sector-specific noise.
Worker-level wage changes are combined with time-series filtering to estimate a persistent wage-inflation trend and its uncertainty interval.
The latent trend is decomposed into an economy-wide component and industry components so broad labor-cost pressure can be separated from sectoral reallocation.
The estimate is surrounded by a sixty-eight percent uncertainty band and can be affected by missing or disrupted source months, so point movements must not be overinterpreted.

variables.name: worker-level wage growth
variables.definition: Individual wage changes used as noisy observations of underlying wage inflation.
variables.provider: U.S. household microdata used by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York

variables.name: Trend Wage Inflation
variables.definition: Estimated persistent component of aggregate wage inflation after filtering transitory worker-level variation.
variables.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

variables.name: common wage trend
variables.definition: Economy-wide latent component shared across industry wage-growth processes.
variables.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

variables.name: industry-specific wage trends
variables.definition: Persistent industry deviations from the common wage-inflation component.
variables.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

variables.name: transitory wage noise
variables.definition: Worker-specific and short-lived wage movements not attributed to the persistent trend.

routes.estimand: persistent common and industry-specific components of observed worker-level wage growth as of each vintage
routes.identification: time-series persistence and cross-industry covariance distinguish common trend, sector trends, and transitory noise
assumptions: worker observations are comparable over time after registered sample controls
latent-state dynamics are stable enough for filtering
missing observations are handled using only information available at the as-of date
routes.sample: worker wage observations and industry assignments available in each monthly real-time vintage
routes.formula: wage_{i,s,t}=common_t+industry_{s,t}+transitory_{i,s,t}; latent states follow registered transition equations
routes.aggregation: labor-cost pressure factor with common and sector-specific evidence kept separately visible

summary: The New York Fed Outlook-at-Risk explainer changes the object of analysis from one central GDP forecast to the entire conditional distribution. Financial conditions and other predictors shift downside and upside quantiles differently, so MacroTrace must expose the tenth-percentile outcome, median, dispersion, and density calibration instead of presenting an uncalibrated recession probability.
question: How should current predictors be translated into the conditional distribution and downside tail of future U.S. growth rather than only its mean forecast?

evidence.paraphrase: The explainer argues that a point forecast omits economically important asymmetry and tail risk contained in the full conditional distribution of future activity.
Predictors such as financial conditions are linked to several future-growth quantiles, which are then represented as a conditional probability distribution.
Examples contrast crisis and tranquil dates to show that similar central forecasts can coexist with very different downside tails and distribution shapes.
A low conditional quantile is a tail outcome rather than a recession probability; extensions to unemployment or inflation require target-specific estimation and calibration.

variables.name: future GDP growth quantiles
variables.definition: Conditional quantiles of future real GDP growth, including the downside tenth percentile and the median.
variables.provider: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and model estimates

variables.name: financial conditions
variables.definition: Observed financial-condition state used to explain asymmetric changes in the future growth distribution.

variables.name: current macro state
variables.definition: Registered activity and inflation controls conditioning the future-growth distribution.

variables.name: conditional growth density
variables.definition: Coherent probability density fitted across the separately estimated conditional growth quantiles.

routes.method: quantile regression plus constrained conditional-density fitting
routes.estimand: conditional quantiles and calibrated density of cumulative future GDP growth at horizon h
routes.identification: predictive conditional distribution; coefficients are not structural causal effects of financial conditions
assumptions: forecast origins are strictly time ordered
quantile specifications are estimated without future revisions
density fitting preserves ordered quantiles and nonnegative probability
routes.sample: real-time U.S. GDP, financial, and macro predictors available at each forecast origin
routes.formula: Q_tau(g_{t+h}|I_t)=alpha_tau+beta_tau FCI_t+gamma_tau' Macro_t; fit registered density across tau
diagnostics: rolling out-of-sample quantile and CRPS loss
routes.aggregation: tail-risk evidence node; only calibrated distribution probabilities may feed numerical recession-risk claims

summary: The San Francisco Fed tariff study uses historical cross-country variation to trace component-level inflation responses after tariff changes. It supports an international panel local-projection node with country effects, macro controls, horizon-specific confidence intervals, and separate energy, goods, services, and core outcomes; the historical average response must remain conditional evidence rather than a mechanical forecast for a new U.S. tariff episode.
question: How do tariff increases affect headline and component inflation over subsequent years, and which price categories carry the response?
horizon: impact through registered annual post-tariff horizons

evidence.paraphrase: The article asks whether tariff increases pass through differently to energy, goods, services, core, and headline consumer-price inflation.
The empirical sample combines annual observations for sixteen countries, largely from the 1980s through 2022, to obtain tariff variation beyond a single episode.
Horizon-specific inflation responses are estimated with country controls, lagged macro-financial variables, and confidence intervals around the response to a tariff increase.

The displayed ten-percentage-point tariff experiment summarizes historical conditional responses and may not transport to a new episode with different retaliation, exchange rates, expectations, or sector coverage.

variables.name: component inflation responses
variables.definition: Headline, energy, goods, services, and core consumer-price inflation observed at each post-tariff horizon.

variables.name: tariff-rate change
variables.definition: Change in the applied tariff measure used as the panel policy shock.

variables.name: lagged macro-financial controls
variables.definition: Past unemployment, inflation, real exchange rates, short rates, equity returns, trade balance relative to GDP, and productivity.

variables.name: country effect
variables.definition: Country-specific time-invariant heterogeneity and registered country trend or time controls.

routes.method: international panel local projections with component outcomes
routes.estimand: horizon-specific change in component inflation following a tariff-rate increase, conditional on registered controls
routes.identification: historical within-country tariff changes conditional on lags, fixed effects, and registered trends
assumptions: conditional tariff innovations are not driven by omitted future inflation shocks
cross-country measurement is comparable
spillovers and retaliation do not invalidate the registered estimand
routes.sample: annual sixteen-country panel, primarily 1980s through 2022, restricted to data available for every registered specification
robustness: alternative country trends and time effects
exclude major tariff episodes one at a time
alternative tariff measures and lag sets
routes.aggregation: causal-scenario evidence node for tariff price pass-through; transportability warning remains attached

summary: Atlanta Fed GDPNow is a component-level nowcast system rather than one black-box GDP regression. It fills missing monthly indicators with a dynamic factor model, maps them into thirteen NIPA GDP subcomponents using bridge equations and Bayesian VARs, and aggregates those forecasts through national-accounts identities. MacroTrace should reproduce that visible DAG, real-time release updates, and accounting reconciliation.
question: How can incoming mixed-frequency U.S. releases be converted into a real-time, component-consistent nowcast of current-quarter real GDP growth?
horizon: current quarter and next released GDP estimate

evidence.paraphrase: The explainer describes a mechanical estimate of current-quarter real GDP growth that updates as source releases arrive rather than relying on discretionary judgment.

evidence.locator: Dynamic factor, bridge, and BVAR stages
evidence.paraphrase: A dynamic factor model fills missing monthly observations, while bridge equations and Bayesian vector autoregressions forecast thirteen GDP subcomponents.
Forecasted subcomponents are combined using national-income accounting identities and contribution arithmetic to produce the top-line GDP nowcast.
The estimate can change materially with new releases and revisions, and a transparent mechanical nowcast can still have substantial error relative to later GDP estimates.

variables.name: real GDP growth nowcast
variables.definition: Model-implied current-quarter annualized growth in real gross domestic product.
variables.provider: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta

variables.name: GDP subcomponent forecasts
variables.definition: Forecasts for thirteen expenditure and inventory components that add up to real GDP growth.
variables.unit: levels, growth rates, and contribution percentage points

variables.name: monthly source indicators
variables.definition: Mixed-frequency activity, spending, housing, trade, inventory, production, and price releases used before the quarter is complete.

variables.name: estimated monthly factors
variables.definition: Latent factors used to fill ragged-edge gaps in the monthly source panel.

variables.name: release news
variables.definition: Difference between a newly observed release and its prior model expectation, propagated through the component DAG.

routes.method: ragged-edge DFM plus component bridge equations and BVARs
routes.estimand: current-quarter real GDP growth implied by information available at each release-time vintage
routes.identification: predictive mixed-frequency system with accounting aggregation; no causal interpretation
assumptions: every release is time-stamped and stored by vintage
monthly-to-quarterly mappings and component identities are fixed by recipe
parameters are estimated only on data available at each historical origin
routes.sample: real-time U.S. source releases and NIPA vintages available at each intraquarter update
routes.formula: monthly panel -> DFM ragged-edge estimates -> bridge/BVAR component forecasts -> NIPA contribution sum = GDP nowcast
diagnostics: rolling real-time RMSE and revision decomposition
robustness: alternative factor counts and lag orders
routes.aggregation: component forecasts aggregate by registered NIPA identities, never LLM weights

summary: The Cleveland Fed inflation-nowcasting page describes a small, deliberately structured mixed-frequency system for current-quarter CPI and PCE inflation. Daily oil, weekly gasoline, and monthly official price releases update headline and core measures, with monthly forecasts aggregated to quarterly rates. The useful product lesson is release-aware component updating and benchmarked real-time error, not the claim that a few market prices explain all inflation mechanisms.
question: How can high-frequency energy prices and partial monthly releases update current-quarter U.S. CPI and PCE inflation before the official quarter is complete?

evidence.paraphrase: The page provides frequently updated model estimates of current-quarter headline and core CPI and PCE inflation before all official observations are released.
The system combines daily oil prices, weekly gasoline prices, and monthly CPI and PCE releases in a compact mixed-frequency information set.
Monthly inflation projections are combined into quarter-over-quarter annualized nowcasts for the corresponding official price indexes.
Disrupted or missing official months require explicit handling, and nowcast quality must be assessed against statistical and survey benchmarks rather than inferred from fit alone.

headline and core equations remain distinct
monthly-to-quarterly compounding follows the official index definition

diagnostics: real-time RMSE and MAE by target
robustness: headline, core, CPI, and PCE target separation
routes.aggregation: inflation-nowcast node with exact temporal aggregation and separate headline/core outputs

summary: The New York Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index compresses transportation-cost and manufacturing-survey indicators into a standardized latent measure of global supply pressure. The construction is valuable as a cost-push factor only if shipping and PMI inputs, demand adjustment, missing observations, normalization, loadings, and pandemic-regime sensitivity remain visible; the index is not itself an identified estimate of U.S. inflation pass-through.
question: What common global supply-chain pressure is contained in transportation-cost and manufacturing-survey indicators, separate from broad demand conditions?
horizon: current global supply state and near-term cost pressure

evidence.paraphrase: The page presents a single measure intended to summarize the common state of global supply-chain pressure across multiple transportation and survey indicators.
Ocean and air freight costs are combined with country-level purchasing-manager measures related to delivery times, backlogs, and purchased stocks.
Standardized indicators are combined through a factor framework, with demand-related influences accounted for so the resulting index is interpreted as supply pressure.
The index is expressed in historical standard deviations, depends on coverage and loading stability, and does not by itself quantify causal pass-through into U.S. consumer prices.

variables.definition: Standardized common factor summarizing global transportation and manufacturing supply-chain pressure.

variables.name: manufacturing supply indicators

variables.name: global demand controls
variables.definition: Registered demand-related survey information removed or controlled so the factor is not merely a global demand index.

variables.name: U.S. inflation outcome
variables.definition: Subsequent U.S. goods or aggregate inflation used only in a separate pass-through model.
variables.provider: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics or U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis

routes.estimand: common standardized supply-chain pressure in the observed shipping and PMI panel
routes.identification: latent-factor extraction after registered demand adjustment; not causal inflation identification
assumptions: standardized inputs share a stable common supply component
input direction and normalization are fixed by recipe
missing indicators and changing country coverage are handled without future information

routes.formula: standardize X_t; remove registered demand component; estimate common factor GSCPI_t=lambda'X_t+e_t
routes.aggregation: external-supply state factor; any U.S. inflation pass-through requires a separate identified or predictive node

summary: The Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE measure is a transparent cross-sectional transform: order monthly PCE component price changes, remove expenditure-weighted tails, and average the remaining mass. The specific lower twenty-four and upper thirty-one percent trims were chosen historically to track underlying inflation, so MacroTrace must preserve component weights, boundary handling, add-up checks, and out-of-sample sensitivity rather than treating the tuning constants as universal truth.
question: What measure of underlying U.S. PCE inflation results when extreme component price changes are removed using expenditure weights each month?
horizon: current month and trailing annual underlying inflation

evidence.paraphrase: The page motivates a PCE inflation measure that reduces the influence of unusually large positive and negative component price changes each month.
Component price changes are sorted and the weighted lower twenty-four percent and upper thirty-one percent of the distribution are removed before averaging.
The remaining component price changes are averaged with PCE expenditure weights, preserving a transparent contribution calculation for the retained mass.
The asymmetric trim fractions were selected from historical fit to proxies for underlying inflation, which creates a tuning choice that requires stability and out-of-sample checks.

variables.name: trimmed-mean PCE inflation
variables.definition: Weighted mean inflation rate of PCE components remaining after registered lower- and upper-tail trims.

variables.name: component price changes
variables.definition: Monthly price change for each detailed PCE consumption component before cross-sectional sorting.

variables.name: component expenditure weights
variables.definition: Current PCE expenditure share assigned to each price component in the cross-sectional distribution.

variables.name: trim boundaries
variables.definition: Registered cumulative expenditure cutoffs at the lower and upper tails, including boundary-component prorating rules.
variables.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas methodology

routes.estimand: monthly underlying PCE price change after removing registered expenditure-weighted tail mass
routes.identification: deterministic robust aggregation rather than causal estimation
assumptions: component prices and expenditures share the same PCE vintage
weights add to the registered aggregate
boundary components are handled deterministically
routes.sample: complete detailed monthly PCE component table for each data vintage
routes.formula: sort component inflation pi_j; trim cumulative weight below 24 percent and above 69 percent; TRIM=sum retained w_j pi_j/sum retained w_j
robustness: median PCE and core PCE benchmarks
routes.aggregation: deterministic factor transform feeding underlying-inflation nodes; no learned cross-lane weight

summary: The Chicago Fed NFCI summarizes 105 weekly financial indicators as a standardized broad conditions index and exposes risk, credit, and leverage subindexes. Its adjusted version removes variation associated with contemporaneous activity and inflation, while positive readings mean tighter-than-average conditions. MacroTrace should keep the raw and adjusted objects separate and expose loading, coverage, normalization, and macro-adjustment diagnostics.
question: What common U.S. financial-condition state is contained in a large weekly panel, and how much remains after accounting for prevailing activity and inflation?
horizon: current weekly financial conditions and near-term transmission context

evidence.paraphrase: The page describes a broad weekly measure intended to capture U.S. financial conditions across money, debt, equity, and traditional and shadow-banking systems.
One hundred five financial variables are standardized and combined into an index whose historical mean is zero and standard deviation is one.
Risk, credit, and leverage subindexes expose the source of movements, while the adjusted NFCI removes variation associated with current activity and inflation.
Positive values mean tighter conditions relative to the historical average, not a structural neutral rate or an automatically causal estimate of future growth effects.

variables.definition: Registered measures used to remove the component of financial conditions associated with current macroeconomic conditions.

summary: The Philadelphia Fed ADS index estimates a high-frequency latent U.S. business-condition state from six indicators arriving at weekly, monthly, and quarterly frequencies. Its real-time vintages and tentacle plot make revisions and ragged-edge uncertainty part of the evidence. MacroTrace should implement it as a mixed-frequency state-space node whose release-by-release state changes are traceable, not as a static descriptive composite.
question: What is the current latent state of U.S. business conditions when weekly, monthly, and quarterly activity indicators arrive asynchronously and are subsequently revised?
horizon: current high-frequency business state and near-term update path

evidence.paraphrase: The page presents a high-frequency business-conditions measure designed to update the current state of the U.S. economy as heterogeneous releases arrive.
Inputs are weekly initial unemployment claims; monthly payroll employment, industrial production, real income less transfers, and real manufacturing and trade sales; and quarterly real GDP.
A state-space framework reconciles asynchronous observations into a common business-condition index and updates the estimate when new or revised data become available.
Archived vintages and the tentacle visualization expose how the contemporaneous state estimate changes as later releases and revisions expand the information set.

variables.name: ADS business conditions index

variables.name: initial unemployment claims
variables.definition: Weekly new claims for unemployment insurance, direction-adjusted as a timely labor signal.

variables.name: monthly activity indicators
variables.definition: Payrolls, industrial production, real personal income less transfers, and real manufacturing and trade sales.
variables.provider: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Federal Reserve, and U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis

variables.name: real GDP
variables.definition: Quarterly real gross domestic product anchoring the broad activity concept at lower frequency.

variables.name: release and revision news
variables.definition: Difference between newly released or revised data and the state-space model expectation under the prior vintage.

assumptions: release calendars and vintages are faithfully reconstructed
measurement loadings and transition dynamics are stable enough for filtering
missing observations enter as ragged edge rather than imputed future values

routes.aggregation: core activity-state node with release-news lineage and vintage uncertainty visible
